RQ1: Tolerability

Sabrina Norwood

15 May, 2026

Deviations from preregistration

  • Tolerability is a 0/1 variable, and is analyzed appropriately as a logistic regression rather than negative binomial as misspecified in the prereg.

Dependencies

library(tidyverse)
library(broom)
library(emmeans)
library(flextable)
library(officer)
library(lme4)
library(knitr)
library(kableExtra)

dir.create("../reports/")
dir.create("../reports/results_rq1_tolerability/")

Load data

df_rq1 <- read_csv("../data/processed/data_processed_behavioral_data_dropout.csv") %>%
  mutate(condition = relevel(factor(condition), ref = "CCC"))

RQ1 model: binary logistic regression (dropout ~ condition)

Preregistration specified negative binomial but dropout is binary — logistic is the correct choice (confirmed by Hanna’s thesis).

model_rq1 <- glm(dropout ~ 1 + condition,
                 data = df_rq1,
                 family = binomial(link = "logit"))

summary(model_rq1)
## 
## Call:
## glm(formula = dropout ~ 1 + condition, family = binomial(link = "logit"), 
##     data = df_rq1)
## 
## Coefficients:
##              Estimate Std. Error z value Pr(>|z|)    
## (Intercept)   0.67513    0.10382   6.503 7.89e-11 ***
## conditionABC -0.06233    0.14872  -0.419    0.675    
## conditionACC  0.03200    0.14592   0.219    0.826    
## conditionBCC  0.19204    0.15005   1.280    0.201    
## ---
## Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
## 
## (Dispersion parameter for binomial family taken to be 1)
## 
##     Null deviance: 2077.8  on 1640  degrees of freedom
## Residual deviance: 2074.7  on 1637  degrees of freedom
## AIC: 2082.7
## 
## Number of Fisher Scoring iterations: 4
# Tidy results with odds ratios and 95% CIs
results_rq1 <- tidy(model_rq1, exponentiate = TRUE, conf.int = TRUE) %>%
  mutate(
    OR   = round(estimate, 3),
    CI   = paste0("[", round(conf.low, 3), ", ", round(conf.high, 3), "]"),
    p    = case_when(p.value < .001 ~ "< .001",
                     TRUE           ~ as.character(round(p.value, 3)))
  ) %>%
  select(Predictor = term, OR, `95% CI` = CI, p) 

results_rq1 |> kable() |> kable_classic()
Predictor OR 95% CI p
(Intercept) 1.964 [1.606, 2.413] < .001
conditionABC 0.940 [0.702, 1.258] 0.675
conditionACC 1.033 [0.776, 1.375] 0.826
conditionBCC 1.212 [0.903, 1.627] 0.201 
write_csv(results_rq1, "../reports/results_rq1_tolerability/model_rq1_results.csv")

# Model fit
chi_sq  <- model_rq1$null.deviance - model_rq1$deviance
df_diff <- model_rq1$df.null - model_rq1$df.residual
p_fit   <- pchisq(chi_sq, df = df_diff, lower.tail = FALSE)
r2_mcf  <- 1 - (logLik(model_rq1) / logLik(update(model_rq1, . ~ 1)))

cat(sprintf("\nModel fit: χ²(%d) = %.2f, p = %.3f, McFadden R² = %.3f\n",
            df_diff, chi_sq, p_fit, as.numeric(r2_mcf)))
## 
## Model fit: χ²(3) = 3.08, p = 0.380, McFadden R² = 0.001

Non preregistered model: discrete-time dropout hazard

Research question shift. The preregistered RQ1 asks whether condition assignment affects total dropouts — an intention-to-treat (ITT) question at the level of the randomised arm. The non-preregistered model below reframes this to a dose-response question: does the current delay length (in seconds) raise the per-week dropout hazard, regardless of which condition produced that dose? This is a different scientific question — closer to the underlying mechanism the study cares about (do longer delays cause people to give up?).

Why a hazard model. The preregistered NB regression on per-condition dropout counts effectively has 4 data points (one per condition) and models no within-condition variation. The logistic model used above is a clear improvement, but still collapses 6 weeks of activity into a single bit per participant. A discrete-time hazard model preserves when people drop out: each participant contributes one row per week-at-risk, with a binary indicator for whether they dropped out that week.

Why delay_secs instead of condition. The covariate of interest is the current delay length in seconds (3s, 6s, or 10s), which varies by condition × week. Treating it as a continuous numeric predictor uses 1 df instead of 3, gaining power if the dose-response is approximately linear. factor(week) is included to absorb baseline weekly hazard (study fatigue, time-since-start), so the delay_secs coefficient captures the marginal effect of dose holding week constant. Note: in this hazard model, identification of delay_secs is largely between-subject (at any fixed week, a participant’s delay is determined by their condition); the within-subject component exists but is limited because the design only ever ramps delay up.

# Person-period dataset: one row per participant × at-risk week.
# Dropout assumed to occur at the start of week (last_week + 1).
# Censored at week 6 if last_week == 6 (no dropout event).
# delay_secs derived from the same rule as Step 5 of data processing.
person_period <- df_rq1 %>%
  mutate(exit_week = if_else(dropout == 1L, last_week + 1L, 6L)) %>%
  rowwise() %>%
  mutate(week = list(seq_len(min(exit_week, 6L)))) %>%
  unnest(week) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  mutate(
    dropped_out = as.integer(week == exit_week & dropout == 1L),
    delay_secs  = case_when(
      condition == "CCC"                  ~ 10,
      condition == "ABC" & week <= 2      ~ 3,
      condition == "ABC" & week <= 4      ~ 6,
      condition == "ABC"                  ~ 10,
      condition == "ACC" & week <= 2      ~ 3,
      condition == "ACC"                  ~ 10,
      condition == "BCC" & week <= 2      ~ 6,
      condition == "BCC"                  ~ 10
    )
  )

cat("Person-periods:", nrow(person_period),
    "\nDropout events:", sum(person_period$dropped_out), "\n")
## Person-periods: 6764 
## Dropout events: 1102
cat("Dropouts by week (should be 0 in week 1 by construction):\n")
## Dropouts by week (should be 0 in week 1 by construction):
person_period |>
  group_by(week) |>
  summarise(n_dropped = sum(dropped_out)) |>
  kable() |> kable_classic()
week n_dropped
1 0
2 554
3 155
4 138
5 125
6 130 
# Drop week 1: by construction it has zero dropout events (earliest possible
# exit_week is 2 because last_week >= 1 for anyone with data). Including it
# causes separation — the intercept is fit at -Inf and the week dummies blow
# up to compensate.
m_hazard <- glm(
  dropped_out ~ delay_secs + factor(week),
  family = binomial(link = "logit"),
  data   = filter(person_period, week >= 2)
)
summary(m_hazard)
## 
## Call:
## glm(formula = dropped_out ~ delay_secs + factor(week), family = binomial(link = "logit"), 
##     data = filter(person_period, week >= 2))
## 
## Coefficients:
##                Estimate Std. Error z value Pr(>|z|)    
## (Intercept)   -0.722535   0.104295  -6.928 4.27e-12 ***
## delay_secs     0.008775   0.016293   0.539     0.59    
## factor(week)3 -1.150998   0.116535  -9.877  < 2e-16 ***
## factor(week)4 -1.106911   0.120663  -9.174  < 2e-16 ***
## factor(week)5 -1.042684   0.132278  -7.883 3.21e-15 ***
## factor(week)6 -0.787395   0.132478  -5.944 2.79e-09 ***
## ---
## Signif. codes:  0 '***' 0.001 '**' 0.01 '*' 0.05 '.' 0.1 ' ' 1
## 
## (Dispersion parameter for binomial family taken to be 1)
## 
##     Null deviance: 5334.5  on 5122  degrees of freedom
## Residual deviance: 5120.8  on 5117  degrees of freedom
## AIC: 5132.8
## 
## Number of Fisher Scoring iterations: 4
# signif() rounds to N significant figures (round() rounds to N decimal
# places, which is useless for very large or very small numbers).
results_hazard <- tidy(m_hazard, exponentiate = TRUE, conf.int = TRUE) %>%
  mutate(
    OR = round(estimate, 3),
    CI = paste0("[", round(conf.low, 3), ", ", round(conf.high, 3), "]"),
    p  = case_when(p.value < .001 ~ "< .001",
                   TRUE           ~ as.character(round(p.value, 3)))
  ) %>%
  dplyr::select(Predictor = term, OR, `95% CI` = CI, p)

# Predicted dropout probability per delay dose (emmeans).
# The model is additive in delay_secs (no dose × week interaction), so the
# OR per second is constant; what varies usefully across doses is the
# absolute predicted weekly hazard. emmeans averages across the week
# dummies to give a marginal predicted probability at each delay level.
em_hazard_by_dose <- emmeans(
  m_hazard, ~ delay_secs,
  at   = list(delay_secs = c(3, 6, 10)),
  type = "response"
) |>
  summary(infer = TRUE) |>
  as_tibble() |>
  mutate(
    `Pr(dropout)` = signif(prob, 3),
    `95% CI`      = paste0("[", signif(asymp.LCL, 3), ", ",
                                signif(asymp.UCL, 3), "]")
  ) |>
  dplyr::select(`Delay (s)` = delay_secs, `Pr(dropout)`, `95% CI`)

em_hazard_by_dose |> kable() |> kable_classic()
Delay (s) Pr(dropout) 95% CI

Hazard-implied per-condition cumulative dropout

The hazard model predicts dropout per week, per delay dose. To put it on the same scale as the preregistered logistic (which predicts whole-study dropout per condition), we chain the per-week hazards using each condition’s actual delay schedule: cumulative dropout by Week 6 is \(1 - \prod_{w=2}^{6}(1 - h(\text{delay}_w, w))\).

Neither model uses a random effect, so both estimates are already marginal (population-averaged) — no Jensen correction needed.

# Each condition's delay schedule across the at-risk weeks (2..6).
condition_schedule <- tribble(
  ~condition, ~week, ~delay_secs,
  "ABC", 2,  3, "ABC", 3,  6, "ABC", 4,  6, "ABC", 5, 10, "ABC", 6, 10,
  "ACC", 2,  3, "ACC", 3, 10, "ACC", 4, 10, "ACC", 5, 10, "ACC", 6, 10,
  "BCC", 2,  6, "BCC", 3, 10, "BCC", 4, 10, "BCC", 5, 10, "BCC", 6, 10,
  "CCC", 2, 10, "CCC", 3, 10, "CCC", 4, 10, "CCC", 5, 10, "CCC", 6, 10
) |>
  mutate(week = factor(week, levels = 2:6))

# Design matrix in the model's parameterisation.
mm <- model.matrix(formula(m_hazard)[-2], data = condition_schedule)

# Point estimates: predicted per-week hazard → cumulative dropout per condition.
beta_hat <- coef(m_hazard)
condition_schedule$hazard <- plogis(as.numeric(mm %*% beta_hat))

cum_point <- condition_schedule |>
  group_by(condition) |>
  summarise(prob = 1 - prod(1 - hazard), .groups = "drop")

# Parametric bootstrap CIs (delta method awkward through the chained product).
set.seed(42)
n_sim     <- 2000
beta_sim  <- MASS::mvrnorm(n_sim, mu = beta_hat, Sigma = vcov(m_hazard))
cum_boot  <- apply(beta_sim, 1, function(b) {
  h <- plogis(as.numeric(mm %*% b))
  tapply(h, condition_schedule$condition, function(hs) 1 - prod(1 - hs))
})
ci <- t(apply(cum_boot, 1, quantile, probs = c(0.025, 0.975)))

em_hazard_by_condition <- tibble(
  condition = rownames(ci),
  prob      = cum_point$prob[match(condition, cum_point$condition)],
  ci_lower  = ci[, 1],
  ci_upper  = ci[, 2]
) |>
  mutate(condition = factor(condition, levels = condition_order)) |>
  arrange(condition)

em_hazard_by_condition_table <- em_hazard_by_condition |>
  mutate(
    `Pr(dropout)` = signif(prob, 3),
    `95% CI`      = paste0("[", signif(ci_lower, 3), ", ",
                                signif(ci_upper, 3), "]")
  ) |>
  dplyr::select(Condition = condition, `Pr(dropout)`, `95% CI`)

em_hazard_by_condition_table |> kable() |> kable_classic()

Combined comparison: Preregistered vs Exploratory at Week 6

dropout_combined <- bind_rows(
  em_pred_rq1 |>
    mutate(
      condition = factor(condition, levels = condition_order),
      estimate  = prob,
      lower     = asymp.LCL,
      upper     = asymp.UCL,
      Analysis  = "Preregistered (logistic, condition contrast)"
    ),
  em_hazard_by_condition |>
    mutate(
      estimate = prob,
      lower    = ci_lower,
      upper    = ci_upper,
      Analysis = "Exploratory (hazard model, dose-response)"
    )
) |>
  mutate(Analysis = factor(Analysis,
                           levels = c("Preregistered (logistic, condition contrast)",
                                      "Exploratory (hazard model, dose-response)")))

p_dropout_combined <- ggplot(dropout_combined,
  aes(x = condition, y = estimate, ymin = lower, ymax = upper,
      colour = Analysis, shape = Analysis, group = Analysis)) +
  geom_point(size = 3, position = position_dodge(0.4)) +
  geom_errorbar(width = 0.2, position = position_dodge(0.4)) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent_format(accuracy = 1),
                     limits = c(0, 1)) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("Preregistered (logistic, condition contrast)"   = "#2166ac",
                                 "Exploratory (hazard model, dose-response)"  = "#d6604d")) +
  scale_shape_manual(values  = c("Preregistered (logistic, condition contrast)"   = 16,
                                 "Exploratory (hazard model, dose-response)"  = 17)) +
  labs(x = "Condition", y = "Predicted Pr(dropout by week 6)",
       title = "RQ1: Cumulative dropout at Week 6 — preregistered vs. exploratory",
       colour = "Analysis", shape = "Analysis") +
  theme_linedraw() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")

p_dropout_combined
